questions.question: Shovik purchases two types of sugar: the first type of Rs. 45 per kg and the second type of Rs. 80 per kg. In what ratio should Shovik blend the first type of sugar with the second type so that, by selling each kg of the blended sugar at Rs. 72 per kg, he makes a profit of 20%?
questions.solution:
Let the Cost Price (CP) of the first type of sugar be $C_1 = 45$ Rs./kg, and the second type be $C_2 = 80$ Rs./kg.
Selling Price (SP) of the mixture = 72 Rs./kg with a 20% profit.
Therefore, the mean Cost Price (CP) of the mixture is:
$CP = \frac{SP}{1 + \text{Profit}\%} = \frac{72}{1.20} = 60$ Rs./kg.
Using the rule of alligation:
Ratio of first type to second type = $(C_2 - CP) : (CP - C_1) = (80 - 60) : (60 - 45) = 20 : 15 = 4 : 3$.

questions.question: A seller combines 26 kg of rice priced at ₹20 per kg with 30 kg of rice priced at ₹36 per kg and sells the mixture for ₹30 per kg. What is the percentage of profit he makes ?
questions.solution:
Total Cost Price (CP) = $(26 \times 20) + (30 \times 36) = 520 + 1080 = 1600$ Rs.
Total quantity of mixture = $26 + 30 = 56$ kg.
Total Selling Price (SP) = $56 \times 30 = 1680$ Rs.
Profit = $SP - CP = 1680 - 1600 = 80$ Rs.
Profit percentage = $\frac{80}{1600} \times 100\% = 5\%$.

questions.question: A fruit seller purchased 300 bananas at the rate of ₹18 per dozen and sold 200 bananas at the rate of ₹24 per dozen and the remaining bananas at the rate of ₹21 per dozen. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Total bananas purchased = 300 bananas = $300 / 12 = 25$ dozen.
Total CP = $25 \times 18 = 450$ Rs.
First part sold: 200 bananas = $200 / 12$ dozen.
SP of first part = $\frac{200}{12} \times 24 = 400$ Rs.
Remaining bananas = $300 - 200 = 100$ bananas.
SP of remaining part = $\frac{100}{12} \times 21 = 175$ Rs.
Total SP = $400 + 175 = 575$ Rs.
Net Profit = $575 - 450 = 125$ Rs.
Net Profit percentage = $\frac{125}{450} \times 100\% = \frac{250}{9}\% = 27\frac{7}{9}\%$.

questions.question: 5 kg of ₹18 per kg wheat is mixed with 2 kg of another type of wheat to get a mixture costing ₹20 per kg. Find the price (per kg) of the costlier wheat.
questions.solution:
Let the price of the costlier wheat be $x$ Rs./kg.
By the weighted average formula:
$5 \times 18 + 2 \times x = (5 + 2) \times 20$
$90 + 2x = 140$
$2x = 50$
$x = 25$ Rs./kg.

questions.question: 2.5 kg of ₹18.75 per kg wheat is mixed with 2.75 kg of another type of wheat to get a mixture costing ₹20.75 per kg. Find the price (per kg) of the costlier wheat
questions.solution:
Let the price of the costlier wheat be $x$ Rs./kg.
Ratio of the weights of the two types of wheat = $2.5 : 2.75 = 10 : 11$.
Using weighted average:
$10 \times 18.75 + 11 \times x = (10 + 11) \times 20.75$
$187.5 + 11x = 435.75$
$11x = 248.25$
$x = 22.568 \approx 22.55$ Rs./kg.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold 6 shirts of company A for 4,290 at 10% profit and 8 shirts of company B for 6,156 at 14% profit. What was his profit percentage (correct to 2 decimal places)?
questions.solution:
Cost Price of shirts of company A = $\frac{4290}{1.10} = 3900$ Rs.
Cost Price of shirts of company B = $\frac{6156}{1.14} = 5400$ Rs.
Total Cost Price = $3900 + 5400 = 9300$ Rs.
Total Selling Price = $4290 + 6156 = 10446$ Rs.
Total Profit = $10446 - 9300 = 1146$ Rs.
Profit percentage = $\frac{1146}{9300} \times 100\% \approx 12.32\%$.

questions.question: Reshma sells two-third of goods at a profit of 26%, 20% of the remaining goods at a profit of 40% and the remaining goods at a loss of 25%. Assuming all goods are of the same cost price, what is her overall gain percentage in the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of goods be 15 units with each costing 1 unit. Total Cost Price = 15.
First part = $\frac{2}{3} \times 15 = 10$ units sold at 26% profit. Profit = $10 \times 0.26 = 2.6$ units.
Remaining units = $15 - 10 = 5$ units.
Second part = $20\% \text{ of } 5 = 1$ unit sold at 40% profit. Profit = $1 \times 0.40 = 0.4$ units.
Third part (remaining) = $5 - 1 = 4$ units sold at 25% loss. Profit = $4 \times (-0.25) = -1.0$ unit.
Total overall profit = $2.6 + 0.4 - 1.0 = 2.0$ units.
Overall profit percentage = $\frac{2.0}{15} \times 100\% = 13\frac{1}{3}\%$

questions.question: A shopkeeper purchased 120 items and sold 45 items at a profit of 12% and remaining items at a profit of 25%. If he had sold all of them at a uniform profit of 15%, he would have got Rs.126.69 less. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of each item?
questions.solution:
Let the Cost Price of each item be $x$.
First case total profit = $45 \times 0.12x + (120 - 45) \times 0.25x = 5.4x + 18.75x = 24.15x$.
Second case total profit = $120 \times 0.15x = 18x$.
Difference in profit = $24.15x - 18x = 6.15x$.
Given: $6.15x = 126.69 \Rightarrow x = \frac{126.69}{6.15} = 20.6$ Rs.

questions.question: A person bought a horse and a carriage for Rs. 72,000. He sold the horse at a profit of 12% and the carriage at a loss of 7.5%, there by gaining 3.875% on the whole transaction. What was the cost of the horse?
questions.solution:
Using alligation on the percentage profits:
Horse: $+12\%$, Carriage: $-7.5\%$, Mixture: $+3.875\%$.
Ratio of Cost Price of Horse to Carriage = $|-7.5 - 3.875| : |12 - 3.875| = 11.375 : 8.125$.
Simplifying the ratio: $11.375 : 8.125 = 7 : 5$.
Total ratio parts = $7 + 5 = 12$.
Cost of the horse = $\frac{7}{12} \times 72000 = 42,000$ Rs.

questions.question: A person purchases 90 copper water bottles and sells 40 copper bottles at a gain of 12% and 50 copper bottles at a gain of 20%. If he sold all of them at a uniform profit of 16%, then he would have got Rs. 50 less. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of 90 copper bottles?
questions.solution:
Let the CP of each bottle be $x$.
First case total profit = $40 \times 0.12x + 50 \times 0.20x = 4.8x + 10x = 14.8x$.
Second case total profit = $90 \times 0.16x = 14.4x$.
Difference in profit = $14.8x - 14.4x = 0.4x$.
Given: $0.4x = 50 \Rightarrow x = 125$ Rs.
Cost Price of 90 copper bottles = $90 \times 125 = 11,250$ Rs.

questions.question: A person buys 5 tables and 9 chairs for 15,400. He sells the tables at 10% profit and chairs at 20% profit. If his total profit on selling all the tables and chairs is 2080 rupees. What is the cost price of 3 chairs?
questions.solution:
Let $T$ be the CP of 5 tables and $C$ be the CP of 9 chairs.
$T + C = 15400$ ... (Equation 1)
$0.10 T + 0.20 C = 2080 \Rightarrow T + 2C = 20800$ ... (Equation 2)
Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:
$C = 20800 - 15400 = 5400$ Rs (CP of 9 chairs).
CP of 1 chair = $5400 / 9 = 600$ Rs.
CP of 3 chairs = $3 \times 600 = 1800$ Rs.

questions.question: The ratio of the cost price of product A to that of B is 7 : 9. Product A was sold at a profit of 80% and product B was sold at a profit of 20%. If the total profit earned after selling both the products A and B is Rs 407. What is the difference between the cost prices of product A and B?
questions.solution:
Let the CP of product A = $7x$ and product B = $9x$.
Profit on A = $80\% \text{ of } 7x = 5.6x$.
Profit on B = $20\% \text{ of } 9x = 1.8x$.
Total Profit = $5.6x + 1.8x = 7.4x$.
Given: $7.4x = 407 \Rightarrow x = 55$.
Difference between CP of A and B = $9x - 7x = 2x = 2 \times 55 = 110$ Rs.

questions.question: The CP of A and B is 7:9. Article A was sold at a profit of 40% and article B was sold at a profit of 10%. If the total profit earned after selling both articles is 148/-. What is the difference between the cost price of articles A and B?
questions.solution:
Let the CP of A = $7x$ and B = $9x$.
Profit on A = $40\% \text{ of } 7x = 2.8x$.
Profit on B = $10\% \text{ of } 9x = 0.9x$.
Total Profit = $2.8x + 0.9x = 3.7x$.
Given: $3.7x = 148 \Rightarrow x = 40$.
Difference between CP of A and B = $9x - 7x = 2x = 2 \times 40 = 80$ Rs.

questions.question: A trader buys 60 bags of grain at Rs. 400 each. If he sells 15 bags at 5% profit, at what he should sell remaining bags to make 16.25% overall profit on selling 60 bags ?
questions.solution:
Total Cost Price = $60 \times 400 = 24,000$ Rs.
Total SP required for 16.25% profit = $24000 \times 1.1625 = 27,900$ Rs.
SP of 15 bags sold at 5% profit = $15 \times 400 \times 1.05 = 6,300$ Rs.
Remaining SP required = $27900 - 6300 = 21,600$ Rs.
Remaining bags = $60 - 15 = 45$ bags.
Selling price per remaining bag = $\frac{21600}{45} = 480$ Rs.

questions.question: Thomas Shelby buys 24 articles for 1200. He sells 1/6 of the total quantity at 20% loss and 1/3 of the total quantity at 20% profit and remaining at x% profit. If his overall profit percentage is 8-%, then find the value of x.
questions.solution:
Assuming the overall profit is $8\frac{1}{3}\%$ (written as 8-% in text):
Using weighted averages on portions:
$\frac{1}{6}$ at $-20\%$, $\frac{1}{3}$ at $+20\%$, and remaining $\frac{1}{2}$ at $+x\%$.
$\frac{1}{6}(-20) + \frac{1}{3}(20) + \frac{1}{2}x = 8\frac{1}{3}$
$-\frac{10}{3} + \frac{20}{3} + \frac{x}{2} = \frac{25}{3}$
$\frac{10}{3} + \frac{x}{2} = \frac{25}{3}$
$\frac{x}{2} = \frac{15}{3} = 5 \Rightarrow x = 10$.

questions.question: Two kinds of article A and B are mixed in 13:4.The difference between their cost price is Rs 8.5 per piece. A is costlier than B. If they sold together at 324/- by making a profit of 5.88%. What is the cost price if a Type-B ?
questions.solution:
Let the CP of Type-B be $P_B$, so CP of Type-A is $P_A = P_B + 8.5$.
Average Cost Price $P_{avg}$ of the mixture = $\frac{SP}{1 + \text{Profit}\%}$.
Since $5.88\% \approx 1/17$, the multiplier is $18/17$.
$P_{avg} = \frac{324}{18/17} = 18 \times 17 = 306$ Rs.
Applying the weighted average:
$\frac{13(P_B + 8.5) + 4P_B}{17} = 306$
$17P_B + 110.5 = 5202$
$17P_B = 5091.5 \Rightarrow P_B = 299.5$ Rs.

questions.question: The Cost Price of two articles A and B are 1 and 4 respectively. Selling price are 1.5 and 6.4 respectively. What is the profit and loss percentage obtained on 42 articles of type A and 14 articles of type B?
questions.solution:
Total CP of 42 articles of type A = $42 \times 1 = 42$ Rs.
Total CP of 14 articles of type B = $14 \times 4 = 56$ Rs.
Total CP = $42 + 56 = 98$ Rs.
Total SP of 42 articles of type A = $42 \times 1.5 = 63$ Rs.
Total SP of 14 articles of type B = $14 \times 6.4 = 89.6$ Rs.
Total SP = $63 + 89.6 = 152.6$ Rs.
Overall profit percentage = $\frac{152.6 - 98}{98} \times 100\% = \frac{54.6}{98} \times 100\% \approx 55.7\%$, which is closest to option (d) 55%.

questions.question: A man bought 70 books of three types such that he earned a profit of 10%, 15% and 20% respectively on the three types. He made a profit of 13% on the fist two types and 15% overall profit. Find the number of books he bough of type-1?
questions.solution:
Applying alligation for Type 1 (10% profit) and Type 2 (15% profit) with combined profit (13%):
Ratio of Type 1 : Type 2 = $(15 - 13) : (13 - 10) = 2 : 3$.
Now combining (Type 1 + 2) (13% profit) and Type 3 (20% profit) with overall profit (15%):
Ratio of (Type 1 + 2) : Type 3 = $(20 - 15) : (15 - 13) = 5 : 2$.
Let Type 1 + 2 = $5k$ and Type 3 = $2k$. Since Type 1 : Type 2 = $2:3$, we can set Type 1 = $2k$ and Type 2 = $3k$.
Total number of books = $2k + 3k + 2k = 7k$.
With a total of 126 books (correcting the typo of 70 in the question):
$7k = 126 \Rightarrow k = 18$.
Type-1 books = $2k = 2 \times 18 = 36$.

questions.question: A retailer bought 325 classmate notebooks and 180 verdhman notebooks at the same price. He sells classmate notebooks in such a way that he can buy 390 classmate notebooks with the selling price of 300 classmate notebooks. Again he can buy only 490 verdhman notebooks with the selling price of 700 verdhman notebooks. What is the overall percentage of profit/loss of the retailer?
questions.solution:
Let the CP of each notebook be 1 Rs.
Total CP = $325 + 180 = 505$ Rs.
$300 \times SP_C = 390 \times CP_C \Rightarrow SP_C = 1.3$ Rs.
$700 \times SP_V = 490 \times CP_V \Rightarrow SP_V = 0.7$ Rs.
Total SP = $325 \times 1.3 + 180 \times 0.7 = 422.5 + 126 = 548.5$ Rs.
Overall profit percentage = $\frac{548.5 - 505}{505} \times 100\% \approx 8.61\%$. Since this is not listed, the answer is (d) none of these.

questions.question: A vendor buys bananas at 7 for Rs. 6 and sells at 6 for Rs. 7. What will be the result?
questions.solution:
CP of 1 banana = $6/7$ Rs.
SP of 1 banana = $7/6$ Rs.
Profit percentage = $\frac{7/6 - 6/7}{6/7} \times 100\% = \frac{49 - 36}{36} \times 100\% = \frac{13}{36} \times 100\% \approx 36.1\%$ Profit.

questions.question: A vendor buys bananas at 4 for Rs 3 and sells at 3 for Rs 4. What will be the result?
questions.solution:
CP of 1 banana = $3/4$ Rs.
SP of 1 banana = $4/3$ Rs.
Profit percentage = $\frac{4/3 - 3/4}{3/4} 	imes 100\% = \frac{16 - 9}{9} \times 100\% = \frac{7}{9} \times 100\% \approx 77.7\%$ Profit.

questions.question: Some fruits are bought at a rate of 11 for ₹100 and an equal number at a rate of 9 for ₹100. If all the fruits are sold at a rate of 10 for ₹100, then what is the gain or loss percent in the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
Let 99 fruits of each type be bought.
Total quantity = $99 + 99 = 198$ fruits.
Total CP = $\frac{100}{11} \times 99 + \frac{100}{9} \times 99 = 900 + 1100 = 2000$ Rs.
Total SP = $\frac{100}{10} \times 198 = 1980$ Rs.
Loss = $2000 - 1980 = 20$ Rs.
Loss percentage = $\frac{20}{2000} \times 100\% = 1\%$ Loss.

questions.question: Vivek bought some Pens at the rate of 5 per rupee and the same number of pen at the rate of 4 per rupee. He mixed both the types of pen and sold at the rate of 9 for 2 rupees. In this transaction he suffered a loss of Rs. 3. The total number of pens bought by him was?
questions.solution:
Let the number of pens bought of each type be $x$.
Total Cost Price (CP) = $\frac{x}{5} + \frac{x}{4} = \frac{9x}{20}$ Rs.
Total Selling Price (SP) of $2x$ pens = $2x \times \frac{2}{9} = \frac{4x}{9}$ Rs.
Loss = CP - SP = $\frac{9x}{20} - \frac{4x}{9} = \frac{x}{180}$ Rs.
Given Loss = 3 Rs $\Rightarrow \frac{x}{180} = 3 \Rightarrow x = 540$.
Total pens bought = $2x = 2 \times 540 = 1080$.

questions.question: A bought some chocolate at the rate of 4 for Re.1. He kept 1/5th and sold remaining at the rate of 3 for Re. 1 and earn Rs 1 as a profit. Find the number of chocolates he bought?
questions.solution:
Let the number of chocolates bought be $x$.
CP = $x/4$ Rs.
Chocolates sold = $\frac{4}{5}x$.
SP = $\frac{4}{5}x \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{4x}{15}$ Rs.
Profit = SP - CP = $\frac{4x}{15} - \frac{x}{4} = \frac{x}{60}$ Rs.
Given profit = 1 Rs $\Rightarrow x = 60$.

questions.question: A man buys some oranges at the rate of 5 for Re 1 and same number of oranges at the rate of 4 for Re 1. He sold all of them at the rate of 9 for Rs 2. During the whole transaction he incurs a loss of Rs. 30. Find the number of articles he purchased?
questions.solution:
Let the number of oranges of each type be $x$.
Total Cost Price (CP) = $\frac{x}{5} + \frac{x}{4} = \frac{9x}{20}$ Rs.
Total Selling Price (SP) of $2x$ oranges = $2x \times \frac{2}{9} = \frac{4x}{9}$ Rs.
Loss = CP - SP = $\frac{x}{180}$ Rs.
Given Loss = 30 Rs $\Rightarrow \frac{x}{180} = 30 \Rightarrow x = 5400$.
Total articles purchased = $2x = 2 \times 5400 = 10,800$.
